answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with stake size setting a capped rate of participation. A sable agent and a falcon agent may both enter the garden, but each must tie its own capital to an auditable record; identities caught coordinating fraud forfeit that stake. This raises the cost of a sybil attack roughly with the number of influential fake agents, while slashing makes detection costly to ignore. It does not prevent wealthy attackers or replace checks against collusion.
